subjects.displayTitle: Discerning companionship: care, influence, and protective boundaries
subjects.introduction: There are people whose conversation revives the withered and rescues the doubting, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes, and others whose very breath puts out the light of faith; association, He adds, is contagious. That is the whole difficulty of companionship: it forms us whether we intend it or not. Bahá’u’lláh tells the seeker to treasure the company of the righteous and shun the ungodly, and in the same writings commands His followers to consort with the followers of every religion in fragrance and joy and to treat even enemies with love. The two instructions are not in conflict once avoidance is understood rightly. There is a withdrawal that protects, done without harshness, censure or slander, leaving the other in the hand of God; and there is a hostility that is forbidden. The Dhammapada’s advice to walk with an equal or a better, or else alone, and its warning that nearness to the wise is not understanding them, sharpen the same discernment [1]. Severe language in some letters belongs to its own circumstances and licenses no label for whole groups. The road leads toward consorting with all, kindness and love to everyone, and the particular case of avoiding Covenant-breakers.
subjects.arc: Begin with the difference between protective distance and hostility, examine formative influence, and bring severe cautions into conversation with universal kindness.

order.why: Open with kindness and the distinction between two forms of avoidance.
shortened: When any of the friends associate with the heedless ones, they should, with utmost kindness and joy, become the cause of their awareness and the means of their remembrance. Avoidance is of two kinds: One kind is to protect the Cause of God, and this should be done with spirit and fragrance, not with harshness and severity. The other kind stems from harshness, and this is not acceptable.

order.why: Explains association with those in error through kindness, guidance and wisdom.
State the command to treat even enemies with love.
shortened: We are commanded to deal with the utmost love and kindness even with our enemies, how much more so with friends.

order.why: Join vigilance with restraint from aggression and backbiting.
shortened: O ye beloved ones, guard the Cause of God! Let no sweetness of tongue beguile you -- nay, rather consider the motive of every soul, and ponder the thought he cherisheth. Be ye straightway mindful and on your guard. Avoid him, yet be not aggressive! Refrain from censure and from slander, and leave him in the Hand of God.

order.why: Recall that religion must not become a cause of hatred.
shortened: From the earliest days until now, this Wronged One's purpose hath been that the religion of God should not become a cause of hatred, and that all should act with and associate with those on earth in a spirit of fragrance and delight, save those souls from whom the odor of malice is diffused - in such case, avoidance is necessary....

order.why: Name both fellowship and avoidance as questions requiring interpretation.
Read the explanation of apparently differing commands.
Give fellowship with Christian friends a concrete setting.
Introduce companionship as nourishment of the heart.
shortened: Treasure the companionship of the righteous and eschew all fellowship with the ungodly.

Give ear unto this: Never shall mortal eye recognize the everlasting Beauty, nor the lifeless heart delight in aught but in the withered bloom. For like seeketh like, and taketh pleasure in the company of its kind.

order.why: Connect wise company with the discipline of the seeker.
shortened: He should be content with little, and be freed from all inordinate desire. He should treasure the companionship of those that have renounced the world, and regard avoidance of boastful and worldly people a precious benefit.

order.why: Make the life-giving effect of conversation tangible.
shortened: There are persons with whom you associate and converse whose utterances are life-imparting, joy-giving. The withered and faded are refreshed, the joyless become happy, the extinct become enkindled and the lifeless are quickened with the breaths of the Holy Spirit.

On the other hand there are some persons whose very respiration extinguishes the light of faith; whose conversation weakens firmness and steadfastness in the Cause of God; whose company divert oneis attention from the kingdom of Abha.

order.why: Read the contrast between righteous and harmful influence.
shortened: This is why one must avoid the wicked and associate with the righteous.
In the Persian Hidden Words He states: "O My son! The company of the ungodly increaseth sorrow, whilst fellowship with the righteous cleanseth the rust from off the heart."

order.why: Ask how association shapes character.
Retain the brief warning about moral corruption.
Place the garden of the heart beside the choice of companions.
shortened: In the Persian Hidden Words it is stated: O Friend! In the garden of the heart plant only flowers of Love, and withdraw not from clinging to the Nightingale of Love and yearning. Esteem the friendship of the just but withdraw both mind and hand from the company of the wicked." It is also stated "O my Son, the company of the wicked increaseth sorrow and the fellowship of the righteous removeth the rust of the mind."

order.why: Read the invitation to sustained fellowship with friends.
Consider the particular counsel concerning supportive company.
shortened: Deliver the enclosed letter to him and say that the assistance and grace of the Divine Unity is conditional upon and dependent on the fellowship of one or two holy souls with perfect wisdom, and avoidance of heedless, hateful persons.

order.why: Connect truthfulness with remembering the divine message.
Examine the qualities proposed as grounds for trust.
shortened: Trust no man save him whose breast hath been dilated by God through the light of faith, whom God hath confirmed in His Religion, and who is severed from all else save God and attracted by His Fragrances.

order.why: Distinguish formal acquaintance from dangerous intimacy.
shortened: But, if you find a soul whose friendship or association is dangerous, which may perchance be the cause of harm to yourself, you should have only a formal acquaintanceship. Be kind and speak with such people not harshly, but leave them alone; do not mix with them. There are many bad people in the world; have nothing to do with them. Do not gossip about them.

order.why: Read the stated distinction between religious fellowship and harmful behavior.
Keep the reported account’s purpose of meeting seekers and the poor.
Consider the test of mutual influence over repeated meetings.
shortened: And in this connection the Tongue of Grandeur declares that if after associating with a person in three gatherings you observe no effect from you upon him, surely withdraw, for an effect from him upon you will become manifest.

order.why: Hear the account of attraction eroded by association.
shortened: For example, it has often been observed that some souls, with the utmost love and attraction and joy and fragrance, associated with materialists and the morally corrupt and became completely worthless and empty. Even in the Holy Land, the Protestants took one or two youth to their homes under the pretext of teaching language, and arranged some improper circumstances such as mixing with women. They nearly caused them to go completely astray through these means.

order.why: Keep the warning about speech that extinguishes devotion.
shortened: In contrast to the above, there are people whose breath will extinguish the fire of devotion, who will turn steadfastness into waywardness and beguile those focused on the Abha Kingdom, which is why it is revealed, "Do not associate with stonehearted."

order.why: Retain the severe characterization in its source setting.
Read the poison analogy as a spiritual comparison.
shortened: The material men of this world are like poison to the spiritual. They are the calamities and inconveniences which a man meets within the worldly life. They are like people who are very much intoxicated and do not understand the bitter taste of the cup, while the conscientious and mindful understand its bitterness.

order.why: Continue the sensory analogy without making a medical claim.
shortened: One may live in a place where there are foul odors and not be weakened by that odor, nor become ill, nor contract any sickness or disease. Likewise with heedless souls who harbor ill will and disease toward the Divine Cause and are unmindful of the Truth. When one associates and sits with such souls, one inevitably inhales foul odors which leave their mark.
One must show utmost love and kindness to the followers of all religions, but if a person is a Baha'i and is of bad character and conduct, one must avoid that person even though he be a Baha'i.

order.why: Consider reputation and conduct together.
shortened: Ponder upon this and understand what it means. One who associates with evil companions loses his reputation and his good name; from being good he becomes bad, from being virtuous he becomes impure, from being holy he becomes depraved. Do not take example from the vicious, do not permit your-selves to be corrupted by the evil-minded.

order.why: Keep the knife-edge image within its reported context.
Read the health analogy as a historical spiritual warning.
Examine the reported children’s example without adopting its group generalization.
shortened: The Iranian children in 'Akka were like angels, but alas, some of them associated with the Arabs or with ill-mannered children. When they argued, all their speech was in Persian, but then they would curse in Arabic since they were not taught similar words in Persian. When they became youth, they associated with non-Baha'is and became totally corrupt. Soon I had no choice but to expel them all.
Therefore I exhort you to protect your children from the evil influence of the wayward.

order.why: Encounter the forceful comparison concerning deviation.
shortened: No one can deny the plain fact that the association of those souls who have deviated from the path of rectitude is harmful. Who will advise you to hug a serpent to your breast or keep a scorpion in your sleeve? We must avail ourselves of the association of the righteous and withdraw our hand and mind from the company of the wickedness.

order.why: Read the appeal to earlier warnings and their interpretation.
Distinguish the particular concern for firmness in the Covenant.
shortened: In light of these blessed utterances and the words of Christ, it is clear and evident that one must associate with souls who are firm in the Covenant and be intimate with the righteous, for an evil companion causes the contagion of evil character, like unto leprosy where it is impossible for one to associate and be intimate with a leper without contracting the disease. This is for protection and preservation.

order.why: Keep the warning about specific disruptive motives.
shortened: Beware, beware of meeting or associating with these corrupt souls, for they have no purpose except self and passion, and no intention except sedition and corruption.

order.why: Retain the named personal case rather than generalizing its judgment.
Read the immediate caution in its particular address.
shortened: And whenever you observe anyone who has the slightest unseemly movement or from whom you detect an unholy fragrance, you must absolutely and immediately shun and avoid them, for harm to the Cause of God lies in association with such ones. For certain souls have appeared who are captives to self and passion yet speak the name of Truth. These souls are worse than deadly poison to the Cause of God. Great caution is necessary.

order.why: Consider hypocrisy as a specific danger.
shortened: And thou, O servant, fear God and associate not with those from whose hearts and souls thou perceivest the winds of hypocrisy, and avoid them and abide under a preserved protection.

order.why: Attend to deception through attractive speech.
shortened: Beware lest thou consort with the deceitful ones. Turn thy face from their faces and thine ears from their melodies, lest thou shouldst inhale the poisonous fumes from their souls and find thyself far removed from the shore of the sea.

order.why: Keep the identification of heedlessness within the demonic imagery.
shortened: O servants! The world is the abode of demons - keep yourselves from approaching them. The demons are the wayward ones who lie in the sleep of heedlessness with corrupt deeds. Their sleep is sweeter than wakefulness, and their death more attractive than life.

order.why: Read the warning concerning aversion to remembrance.
Retain the text’s contrast between religious allegiances.
Keep the personal instruction to follow a brother’s example.
Connect the instruction with its appeal for divine preservation.
Hear the particular warning against aversion.
shortened: However, it behooveth thee not to turn to those from whom thou perceivest the fragrance of aversion, nor to draw near unto them, nor to associate with them. Thus have We commanded Our servants who have believed in God, the Almighty, the Most Powerful, the All-Wise.

order.why: Keep the two selected warnings together in their source.
shortened: When you see one who is immersed in his desires, listen not to what he says.
O My creation, behold Me!" When you detect from anyone the fragrance of aversion, draw not near to him - thus does the Lord of the seen and unseen command you.

order.why: Read the differing responses to receptivity and turning away.
shortened: When ye behold those on whose faces shineth the light of the All-Merciful, remind them of this momentous News. And when ye find those who have turned away, avoid them and remain in an impregnable fortress.

order.why: Preserve the succinct contrast concerning loved ones and enemies.
shortened: Associate with My loved ones and shun Mine enemies. Thus doth the Pen of might and glory command thee.

order.why: Read whispering and rebellion as the passage’s spiritual language.
shortened: Unite with the loved ones of God and shun the devils who whisper in the breasts of men and call them to rebellion. By God! They are but in manifest error.

order.why: Attend to the specific condition of known hatred.
shortened: And God's greatest commandment is that association with those souls known for their hatred of the Truth is never permitted. Therefore shun them that you may prosper.

order.why: Keep the counsel addressed to the recipient and fellow believers.
shortened: We counsel thee and those who have believed in that which hath been sent down in the Book of God, the King of this wondrous Day: Shun those who have turned away and consort with My servants who have turned towards Me.

order.why: Observe the stated exception concerning championing the Cause.
shortened: O Majid!
Consort not with Mine enemies, nor turn thy attention unto them, save when thou arisest to champion My Cause.

order.why: Preserve the source’s unusual wording without silently harmonizing it.
shortened: And if thou findest the people heedless of the Cause and intoxicated with love, turn away from them and set thy face toward God.

order.why: Consider the passage’s distinction concerning accompanying others.
shortened: Draw not nigh unto those who have wronged lest their torment touch thee, for they have no life in them. Walk with them toward thy goal, for this is permitted to the believers in the Book of God."

order.why: Close linked readings with examination of love within one’s own heart.
shortened: And if thou findest in thy heart My love, then cleave unto it; otherwise, keep aloof therefrom and be of those who turn aside.

order.why: Read the supplied report’s distinction between harms to oneself and to others.
shortened: Question: 'How should one associate with people of bad character?'

There are certain evils whose consequences affect the doer only and do not extend to others. Of course, with discretion and tact, we must try to warn and educate wrongdoers. They are sick; we must bring healing to them. But there are actions which are injurious to others. Association with persons who commit such deeds leads to a deterioration of morals and therefore to mingle with them is not advisable, except for persons of perfect integrity, who can also impart education.

references.note: Acharya Buddharakkhita’s translation advises seeking an equal or better companion, or traveling alone; it then contrasts awareness of one’s folly with imagined wisdom, and mere proximity to a wise person with actual understanding. Read the spoon and tongue images beside the compilation’s accounts of influence.
